newsitem.title: UK: Chiroscience in U.S. asthma pill pact.
newsitem.headline: Chiroscience in U.S. asthma pill pact.

text.p: Chiroscience Group Plc said Friday it agreed to work with Schering-Plough Corp. to develop a new class of pills to treat asthma and other diseases.
Chiroscience said it stood to receive up to $38 million from the deal, mostly in the form of milestone payments, with about $2 million of that allotted for research and development.
The company will also receive royalties on product sales, while Schering, which is based in Madison, N.J., would receive exclusive worldwide rights to all products from the collaboration.
"This agreement comes at an optimum time for our programme -- just as planning for large-scale trials in asthma patients is beginning," said Chiroscience Chief Executive Dr. John Padfield.
The deal should also help boost Chiroscience's results this year, he told Reuters in an interview.
The drug discovery company said the agreement aimed to build on Chiroscience's preliminary success in treating asthma with a compound called D4418, part of a group known as PDE IV inhibitors.
These inhibitors suppress the body's reaction to foreign substances during asthma attacks.
"Asthma is an overreaction to a challenge, and what these compounds do is dampen down that overreaction," director of development Brian Gennery said.
Unlike conventional asthma medicines, the inhibitors would be administered as a pill rather than through aerosol inhalers.
